recipes.name: Easy Apple Coffee Cake
ingredients_raw: 1 (3.4 ounce) package instant vanilla pudding mix

steps.text: Preheat the oven to 350 degrees F (175 degrees C). Grease and flour a 10-inch Bundt pan.
Stir cake and pudding mix together in a large bowl. Add sour cream, eggs, and oil; mix until well blended. Combine sugar, walnuts, and cinnamon medium bowl.

Pour 1/2 of the batter into the prepared pan; layer with 1/2 of the sliced apples; sprinkle with 1/2 of the cinnamon-walnut mixture. Pour remaining 1/2 of the batter over top; layer with the remaining 1/2 of the apples and cinnamon-walnut mixture.
Bake in the preheated oven until a toothpick inserted in cake comes out clean, 60 to 70 minutes. Cool for 30 minutes before removing from the pan to cool completely.

raw_recipe.headline: Easy Apple Coffee Cake
raw_recipe.description: This easy apple coffee cake recipe bakes up into an apple cake with a beautiful layer of fruit in the center. Serve it warm with a scoop of ice cream.

review.reviewBody: Make this exactly as written and I promise you, you won't be disappointed. Use ALL the apples called for, bake about 65 minutes, and cover it the last 10 minutes or so with foil if it starts to get too brown. Those who say this has no flavor must not be using enough apples, which would surely change the taste and texture of this "cake." Just to dress it up, I drizzled it with a simple powdered sugar glaze. This is one darn good apple cake, densely apple-y and incredibly good. Sent it to the office with hubby and he reported his staff were all in apple heaven!

Had to share what I changed in case others are in my situation! I used a Pillsbury Classic Yellow (only 15.25 oz) and sugar free/fat free jello vanilla instant pudding mix (1 oz). I used Greek nonfat plain yogurt instead of sour cream. It was a very thick batter. I only used 2 large gala apples (I definitely could've added more). I only used half the sugar (sweet apples). I cooked in a ceramic bundt pan on convection in my Breville Smart Oven and it was perfect at 65 minutes (I covered the top with foil the last 20 minutes to keep from burning). This came out so well even with my modifications! Thank you!

I agree with some of the other reviews, this took a long time to bake. I don't know if it's because I baked mine at 325 (I used a dark tube pan). I changed a couple of things...I used a vanilla cake mix and sugar-free vanilla instant pudding. I used 5 large Gala apples. I read they are sweeter than Granny Smiths so I sliced them and mixed them with 1 TBL of lemon juice and half a cup of white sugar and 1 tsp of cinnamon. I layered the apples as directed and poured the juice from the apples on the top layer. I had no problem getting the cake out of the pan and it didn't break when I flipped it over. The true test will be when I cut the cake. It smells so good, I can't wait to eat it!

I made this cake this morning. Since a cake mix was used, am I’m gluten free, I use a gluten free cake mix. The mix was too dense, so I added 3/4C of sugar free applesauce. Followed the recipe exactly. It took 1 1/2 hours plus to bake (105 minutes) it was perfect! Not too sweet. I did drizzle it with a glaze and add a few orange sprinkles for ‘presentation ‘! It was delicious. My son said next time to add a Carmel drizzle. This was time consuming, but worth it.

i just took this cake out of the oven and it is delicious! i followed the recipe pretty much "as written" with only a few changes because of the country in which i live: since one can't get sour cream here, i substituted low-fat, plain yogurt that i had drained a little beforehand...probably doing that cut out A LOT of fat grams too! also, since i didn't have a bundt pan, i baked it in a 9x13. since italians like their cakes a little on the "dry side", i baked it for about 1.5 hours at 350 and it didn't burn. (my oven is tiny and LAME!) like another reviewer suggested, i finely chopped the apples and i did use all 6 (of various sizes) with no problems. other than those few changes i thought it was a GREAT recipe! ***the one thing i would recommend is to have all your ingredients ready BEFORE you start mixing the batter. i waited too long (chopping the apples) and had a lot of difficulty spreading the batter in the pan. the pudding makes it very thick.***

Made this for a dinner party. I had a bunch of apples that I needed to use. Read a lot of reviews and decided to grate the apples instead and mixed them with nuts & sugar. Followed directions and made the layers. I used pecans instead of walnuts.When I combined the apples with sugar mixture it got a little watery ( threw away watery part) so I sprinkled sugar and a few more pecans on top before baking. I sifted confectionery sugar on top after it cooled to make it look nice. Cover w foil after 60min. Baked another 10min . Apples baked into cake for a moist delicious dessert. Served w vanilla ice cream. Was a big hit! FYI used organic raw sugar. Don't be concerned that batter is so thick apples cooking in make this an awesome cake!

May just replace my MILs apple cake recipe. :D Delicious with the minor changes suggested from other reviewers: 1) Instead of 1/2 c. white sugar, I used 1/4 c. white and 1/4 c. brown; 2) Instead of 1/2 c. oil, I used 1/4 c. applesauce and 1/4 c. oil; 3) add powdered sugar glaze. For the apples, I used 7 (smaller) apples from my tree which was 4 cups of coarsely chopped apples and that worked well. I tossed the apples in the sugar/nut mixture and folded all of them into the batter. This seemed to give an even distribution of apples through the cake. The cake was baked through after 60 minutes and I did not need foil to prevent the cake from burning.

Just made this today and like many who have reviewed it, I chopped the apples and mixed them with the cinnamon and 1/2 cup of brown sugar. I folded some of the apples into the batter and did thinner layers of apples throughout the cake batter ( batter, apple, batter, apple). I also pressed the apple into the batter a bit. Maybe because of my newer gas oven, I didn't have to bake for the full 60 mins suggested. A toothpick came out clean at approximately 45 mins. I sprinkled powered sugar and caramel sauce on the top for additional flavor and looks. We haven't tried it yet, but if the smell is any indication, my apple loving partner will adore it!

I read the other reviews so I incorporated some of the ideas! However, I pretty much followed the recipe with the exception of adding a bit of brown sugar in my sugar mix. My crew generally don’t like apple cakes but this won them over! I made a delicious Carmel glaze that literally made this a 5 star sensational recipe!

I made this twice. The first time I made it exactly as written and it was amazing. The second time, I chopped the apples and tossed them with the cinnamon mix and folded them into the batter. I made sure to fold loosely, not mix in thoroughly. I prefer the second method because it makes a slice that is easier to cut without falling apart and has a pretty swirl design. Either way is delicious though!

Fabulous! And, as the title states - EASY! You'd never know that the base was a cake mix. I used a french vanilla cake mix and french vanilla pudding mix along with a generous splash of vanilla extract to be sure the cake mix flavor wouldn't come through. And while it did seem like a lot of apples - I'm glad I did use them all because it really made a difference. I tossed the apples in the cinnamon sugar mix along with the walnuts. This came out moist, nicely spiced and chock full of delicious apples. I opted to do a vanilla glaze over top to make it pretty and let it set in the fridge overnight. This was perfect to take over to my mother-in-law's house and was a big hit especially when you cut into it and there is a wonderful thick layer of apples sandwiched in between fluffy vanilla cake. Perfect with a cup of tea or coffee!
We used a butter yellow cake, and sprinkled powdered sugar lightly on top. My family loved this cake.
I have followed this exact recipe for several years. It's amazing!!

This cake was so moist and flavorful it was amazing. I did take a tip and chopped up the apple tossed with cinnamon sugar mixture and then folded them into the batter. I really enjoyed the flavor and because I have a toddler grandson felt chopped apples would be more appropriate . Thanks for amazing recipe oh also it took 45 minutes to bake but my oven runs hot but suggest keeping eye on it😊
This cake is absolutely delicious! I made no changes.
IT was easy and simple. did not need 6 apples. or maybe the grannies I got were to big. only needed 4 to do the job. but it was a hit at the office. and used a simple glaze with apple juice.
I followed there joe as written! It is delicious! Will be making this again!
Super easy. Made this for a church function and it was a hit. I used Granny Smith apples
Will make this again. Tasted like a scratch recipe. Dense moist cake. A hit with my guests /shared the recipe too.

This recipe is definitely a keeper. I did follow everything in the recipe as stated except I put in more cinnamon and nuts. I used pecans because those are my families favorites. There were no leftovers from this cake so I will be make it again especially during apple season.
